core_obligations: Show that the differentials of the variables generate: prove by induction on the total degree that the differential of any polynomial is an S-linear combination of them, splitting a product with the Leibniz rule (proof lines 34534-34544).

Show there are no relations: use the partial derivative derivations, which correspond by the universal property to S-linear maps on the module of differentials sending one variable differential to 1 and the others to 0 (proof lines 34547-34553).
Conclude that the variable differentials form a basis (proof lines 34554-34555).
proof_roadmap: Generate the differentials inductively by degree with the Leibniz rule (proof lines 34533-34544).
Kill relations using the partial derivative functionals (proof lines 34546-34556).
difficulty_reason: For the polynomial ring S = R[x_1, ..., x_n] the lemma states that the module of relative differentials is free with basis the differentials of the variables (statement lines 34526-34531). The proof does not quote a general computation of differentials: it proves generation by an induction on the total degree using the Leibniz rule, and it proves freeness by manufacturing, from the partial derivative derivations, S-linear maps on the module of differentials that isolate each basis element (proof lines 34533-34556). Using the universal property to get the dual functionals is the step that kills all relations, and the author writes both halves out. H2.
